- **Type:** gp3, 200 GiB, attached to `i-1234567890abcdef0_2` as `/dev/sdg`
- **Current IOPS:** 6,000, with throughput at 250 MiB/s
- **Last change:** raised from 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s to 6,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s on 2026-11-11. That change completed.

**10,000 IOPS is valid for this volume.** gp3 allows up to 16,000 IOPS. A 200 GiB volume can go well past 10,000, since gp3 allows up to 500 IOPS per GiB. If you raise IOPS this far, check the throughput setting too. 250 MiB/s may cap you before you reach 10,000 IOPS, depending on your I/O size.

**You can make the change yourself.** Run this with the AWS CLI or console:

`aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --iops 10000 --region us-east-1`

The volume stays attached and usable while it changes. You can only modify a volume once every 6 hours, and the last change was 12 days ago, so that limit won't block you.

**It's worth confirming that IOPS is the bottleneck first.** I can check the volume's CloudWatch metrics (VolumeReadOps, VolumeWriteOps, VolumeQueueLength, and the throughput-exceeded checks) to see whether it's hitting the 6,000 IOPS ceiling.
